label: early original-phase step (t=2-5) after a prefix rich in s/z/w/l/n
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99% of mass), at steps t=2-5 (peak t=3-4). It never fires at t=0-1, at <DEL>, and almost never in the copy phase. It is driven by an early prefix that contains the tokens s, z, w, l, n: prev_tok and prev2_tok in that set give 4-6x lift, and first_tok s/w/z gives 3-4x. Requiring at least two of these among earlier inputs, at t=2-5, covers about 74% of activation mass and 64% of activations on dev, but precision is only about 0.24. Magnitude depends strongly on the current input token. x is by far the strongest (6.7x lift, 26% of mass, and all top activations are x right after a prefix like s s s or s z w), followed by l, f, c, r, n and digits 0/1. Inputs on the first occurrence of a token account for 90% of mass. Activation drops as more digits appear in the sequence. This looks like a graded linear readout of prefix composition times input identity, so a single boolean predicate does not capture it fully.
